title: Singing 'I've Been Hoodooed' in the Overton minstrel show
summary: Love recalls the song in old minstrel shows, with Billy Kersands doing the vest-stripping act on the Overton and Senior Ragtime Minstrel Show trip through Mississippi around 1916.

venues.name: Overton and Senior Ragtime Minstrel Show

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: But this this song when I was telling you about this now I've been hoodoo. They used to sing that in all them old ministry shows long while ago. 1903. Billy Cassand used to sing that in his ministry. You remember you heard of Billy Cassand? Oh sure. Of course he's a famous man. I went I was waiting for a little show they called Overton and Senior Ragtime Minister Show. And he was he just had got by and he went on a honeymoon trip. He just went out with the show. Opened up the show. And he he thought about Bill Cassand you know. His son got Bill Cassand and his wife because they had never went in the state of Mississippi. And he got about $400 a week. We had a ragtime ministry show, you know. And he used to use that number then. That was about 1903. I've been hoodooed. At the end of his song, he would start to pull off his vests, you know. He was a great big fan. He had about, looked like about 50 of them vests on, loud vests, you know. And the last one would be a corset. A lady's corset. And he'd on fast and that, you know. And then he'd grab his suspenders and his wife would catch him, you know. Catch him and bring him off the stage, you know. The old fella tore his last. I made the last trip with him in Mississippi. Let me see what year that was. I can't think of the exact year. Trying to think, no.
Oh, yeah. Way before that. Nineteen. Around 1916 or something like that.
Just before we got in the war then, huh?
